chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥusayn, from his father ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about nosebleeding, cupping, and vomiting. He said: These do not invalidate anything of the wudu (ablution), but they do invalidate the salat (prayer).

key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the ritual prayer whose validity is affected here

ai.seo_question: Do nosebleeding, cupping, or vomiting break wudu (ablution) or salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that nosebleeding, cupping, and vomiting do not invalidate wudu (ablution). However, they do invalidate the salat (prayer), indicating a distinction in fiqh between what breaks ritual ablution and what interrupts the validity of prayer.
